strengths: Novel problem formulation: First framework providing formal robustness guarantees for circuit discovery under dataset perturbations, directly addressing a documented limitation in prior work
Theoretically sound: Properly adapts RS-Del and component-wise certification to circuit discovery with correct proof and well-derived certified radius formula
Comprehensive experimental validation: Thorough evaluation across 5 datasets, 3 scoring functions, 2 architectures with consistent improvements (up to 12% on ImageNet, 91% on OOD data)
Strong empirical results: Certified circuits are simultaneously more compact (45% fewer neurons) and more sufficient/accurate, not trading one property for the other
Algorithm-agnostic framework: Wraps any black-box discovery algorithm, demonstrating broad applicability across different scoring functions
Clear presentation: Well-motivated problem, clearly explained methodology, comprehensive figures and tables
Structural stability analysis: IoU experiments (Figure 4) show certified circuits converge to similar structures on OOD data, supporting the interpretability hypothesis
Additional quality metrics: Appendix C provides class-specificity analysis (oACC) showing certified circuits achieve 99% lower off-target accuracy
weaknesses: Modest certified radius: With chosen parameters (p_del=0.6, τ=0.95), certified radius r=1 guarantees stability only against single-example edits. While theoretically covering exponentially many datasets, practical guarantee is limited

Limited architectural scope: Evaluation restricted to ResNet-50/101 on ImageNet classification. No experiments on Vision Transformers, language models, or other modalities despite claiming algorithm-agnosticism
Computational overhead not thoroughly analyzed: Method requires 1000 discovery algorithm runs, but no timing comparisons provided. Impact on practitioners unclear despite offline assumption
Causal link not rigorously established: Connection between dataset-edit stability and actual spurious feature suppression relies on correlation with OOD performance rather than direct causal evidence
Concept dataset design limitations: All experiments use ImageNet class-as-concept. Sensitivity unexplored: effects of dataset size, subset selection, and non-class concepts not evaluated
Monte Carlo estimation conservatism: Union bound over all |V| vertices could be conservative for large networks; tightness analysis absent
Incomplete concurrent work comparison: Brief reference to Anonymous (2026) providing concurrent guarantees but differences in scope and tradeoffs not thoroughly characterized
Limited ablation studies: Beyond Figure 5, sensitivity to hyperparameter choices (p_del, τ, n) not thoroughly explored
Code not provided: Promised 'soon' but unavailable for review, limiting reproducibility assessment

strengths: Addresses well-motivated, important problem in mechanistic interpretability with formal guarantees—rare in the field
Rigorous theoretical foundation with correct application of randomized smoothing to circuit discovery (Theorem 3.1)
Algorithm-agnostic framework applicable to any circuit discovery method
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 3 architectures, 2 modalities, 4 algorithms, 5 OOD shifts, statistical significance testing
Strong practical improvements: up to 56% accuracy gains on hard OOD shifts, 80% circuit sparsity reduction, structural stability (IoU=0.973 across seeds)
Excellent presentation with clear motivation, effective visualizations (Figures 1-6), detailed experimental setup, and pseudocode algorithms
Honest treatment of limitations; balanced impact statement acknowledging partial explanations
Proper isolation of certification benefits via majority vote baseline (Figure 16) at matched compute
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contribution combines two existing methods (RS-Del + SegCertify) in a relatively straightforward way
Threat model mismatch: edit distance treats all edits equally and doesn't directly capture semantic equivalence of dataset perturbations as claimed
Very conservative certified radii for vision (r=1 only). Large radii require |Dc|≥500+ examples, exceeding typical ImageNet class sizes
Unclear mechanistic source of improvements: abstention aggressively removes ambiguous components; unclear if gains come from better concept capture vs. feature denoising
Missing causal validation: no ablation showing that forced inclusion of abstained neurons actually degrades OOD performance, confirming spuriousness
Limited language task diversity: only 3 synthetic tasks (IOI, IOI-Hard, Greater-Than), all same structure; no large language models tested
Hyperparameter selection process underspecified: Table 2 reports τ, pdel per task but selection procedure, search space, and selection criterion not fully detailed
Concurrent related work exists (Hadad et al., 2026 on neural network verification for circuits), suggesting problem space being explored by others

strengths: Addresses genuine, well-documented problem in circuit discovery: instability to dataset variations; first work to formally certify circuit stability under dataset perturbations
Theoretically sound with Theorem 3.1 correctly combining RS-Del and component-wise certification; proof is rigorous and properly handles FWER; certified radius derived formally
Algorithm-agnostic framework validated across 3 architectures (ResNet, ViT, GPT-2), 2 modalities, multiple discovery algorithms (top-K variants and EAP-IG)

Comprehensive experimental validation: ImageNet + 4 OOD datasets, multiple metrics (sufficiency, compactness, OOD generalization, structural stability), ablations with theoretical analysis (App. C.1-C.2), significance testing

Rare accuracy-robustness trade-off in right direction: certified circuits are simultaneously more accurate AND more compact (up to 56% accuracy gains, 80% fewer components); majority vote comparison isolates τ's contribution
Strong OOD generalization with structural convergence: circuits remain stable when re-discovered on shifted distributions (Fig. 6), suggesting method captures transferable mechanistic structure

Excellent reproducibility: explicit hyperparameters (Table 2), runtime analysis (2.4× optimized overhead), theoretical minimum sample complexity (53-154 samples sufficient), feature visualizations showing spurious feature removal
Stability across seeds demonstrated rigorously (Fig. 11: IoU > 0.95 across 40 independent runs, mean 0.973 ± 0.0015)
weaknesses: Conservative threat model: edit distance does not formally capture semantic equivalence; datasets at edit distance 1 could differ drastically semantically; connection between dataset robustness and true concept understanding assumed rather than proven

Limited practical radius for main application: vision results use conservative r=1 (only 1 dataset edit); larger radii require substantial concept datasets (|D|≥500-1000 for r≥11, Fig. 13-14); most vision tasks use |D|=50

Limited technical novelty: core contribution applies existing techniques (RS-Del + component-wise certification); no new robustness certification methods; incremental conceptual insight rather than methodological innovation

Hyperparameter selection requires tuning: two key parameters (pdel, τ) need per-domain selection; theoretical dependencies characterized (App. C.1) but practical guidance lacking; vision uses fixed values while language uses per-task tuning (Table 2)

Insufficient baseline comparisons: primary comparison to uncertified versions of same algorithm; no comparison to ensemble methods, alternative discovery algorithms, or circuit compression literature; majority vote baseline (F.5) helpful but limited

Abstention mechanism underexplored: components with ⊘ excluded from circuit but semantic interpretation unclear; feature visualizations anecdotal; lack of quantitative analysis of which feature types systematically abstain across many classes

Dataset size dependency limits applicability: method requires sufficient concept data; small |D| common in interpretability work; inherent trade-off between certification strength and base algorithm performance limits practical adoption for data-scarce settings
Language OOD construction uses manually inserted distractors (Table 3) rather than natural distribution shifts; less compelling than vision's real OOD datasets; may not reflect deployment scenarios
Statistical rigor incomplete: Table 1 (main vision results) lacks error bars or significance markers; only Table 5 includes these; strengthens claims but inconsistent reporting across key results

Limited analysis of failure cases: ImageNet-O shows unexpectedly high variance in structural stability (Fig. 6) compared to other OOD shifts; class-dependent instability deserves deeper investigation and explanation
